name: James Rennell Rodd
bio: Poet and diplomat, later British Ambassador to Italy (1908-19) and first Lord Rennell of Rodd. A friend of Wilde at Oxford, where he won the Newdigate Prize in 1880, two years after Wilde. Wilde wrote the 'envoi' to his Rose Leaf and Apple Leaf (1882) and published, as its dedication, an inscription Rodd had written privately in Wilde's own copy — 'TO OSCAR WILDE— HEART'S BROTHER' — which Rodd found much more effusive than he had intended, and which helped end the friendship.
bio_note: Dates 1858-1941 and the biography are from the editors' note 4 at Complete Letters (2000), printed 102. Only one letter to Rodd survives in the volume, headed 'To Rennell Rodd' at printed 102-103. It sits in the same register the Complete Letters reading gives 'warm, and not desire' for Sherard's dedication. Ellmann's one suggestive line - that the two travelled under false names 'presumably to keep Rodd's friends from suspecting that their intimacy was so constant' - is flagged by Ellmann himself as a presumption, and the editors' own note at printed 101 says the travelling companion was 'almost certainly Rennell Rodd', which is a second hedge on top of the first.
